description: Made ground the OS five-foot plan (1891-96) does not level: platforms raised above the marsh, with the evidence for their height. scripts/build_main_landscape.py raises the drawn ground to each (raise only; never inside the drawn river, tidal or ditch water). Levels are ODN metres; scene y = ODN - 1.83544.

platforms.name: Abbey Mills Pumping Station yard (Metropolitan Board of Works, 1865-68)

outline.sourceNote: the main building, traced from the OS five-foot plan
outline.method: The yard round the building: the 2003 ground stays within 0.2 m of level to 15-20 m from its walls on every side, then falls.

platforms.sideGradientNote: Horizontal metres per metre of fall from the yard edge to the marsh. The 2003 ground falls about 0.6 m between 15 and 35 m from the walls; the 1893 plan draws no bank hatching round the station, so the fall is a gentle made-ground slope, not an embankment.
platforms.method: Environment Agency LiDAR DTM (1 m, flown 22 February 2003, tile DTM_V0027976, reference/topography-research-2026-09-28/tiles-2003/TQ3580.zip) round the building footprint: median 3.98 m ODN within 4 m of the walls, 3.91 m at 4-10 m, 3.80 m at 10-20 m and 3.34 m at 20-35 m; 3.78-4.03 m on each side within 10 m. Assumes the 1868 yard is unchanged (author, 6 October 2026: the station stands on the same foundations).
evidence: 2003 LiDAR against the 1890s OS readings within 550 m of the station: the street readings on Abbey Lane and by the gasworks agree within 0.25 m (7 readings; Abbey Road at Abbey Mill, raised later, is 1.1 m higher); the sewer bank top 9.27 against 9.24 m. The marsh readings at the Mill Meads edge are 1.8-4.4 m higher in 2003: later fill (the author: Prescott Channel spoil), so Mill Meads in 2003 is not evidence for the 1890s.
A later OS plan (post-war, LCC Sewage Pumping Station) draws a hachured bank between the station grounds and the Mill Meads allotments (author, 6 October 2026).

Author, 6 October 2026: the Metropolitan Board's engineers knew the marsh flooded and built the station above it; no account of the Abbey Mills station flooding has been found. The 1888 'pumping station' flooding was probably West Ham's own station beside Bow Creek.

boundingReadings.what: Abbey Lane north of the station, OS 1893 street readings
Mill Meads marsh, OS 1893 marsh readings at its edge
Northern Outfall Sewer bank top at the Channelsea, OS 1893

platforms.name: Abbey Mills coal sidings and lead (track bed)

outline.method: Every traced track, 2.5 m either side of its centre line (a single-track bed about 5 m wide); the fan's beds overlap into one yard.

profile.method: Level with the station yard (3.95 m) through the fan, to x -100; rising evenly (about 1 in 72) to the quay at 4.9 m, the OS bank and wall tops along the Channelsea there (4.91 m); level along the quay. Points off the lead take the level at their nearest point on it.

platforms.method: 2003 EA LiDAR along the traced sidings: 3.86-4.29 m ODN through the fan (yard level, as round the engine house). East of x -90 the 2003 ground is a later earthwork (8.7-9.6 m), and the quay is 4.8-5.7 m; the model's quay fill already stands at about 5.0 m.
evidence: The 1893 plan draws no bank hatching along the sidings or the lead: made ground at yard level, not an embankment.
